clue.text: Strident daughter in tirade after party

indicators.note: after places the tirade-with-daughter piece behind the party word in the answer

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: in says the daughter's letter goes inside the word for tirade

parts.note: a rant is a tirade, an angry outburst

explanation.surface: A daughter shrieks through an angry outburst after a party has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harsh and jarring in sound is out of harmony, so a strident voice clashes.

clue.text: X y !

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten and y is the usual abbreviation for year or years

explanation.walkthrough: With no definition, the whole clue is a picture: X stands for ten and y for years, and ten years is the answer. The exclamation mark flags the oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: A span of ten years is the standard meaning of the word, as in the nineteen-sixties.

clue.text: Summer perhaps when boy goes to the briny

parts.note: the briny is a jocular name for the sea
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad heads off to the seaside in the summer holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer is one of the four quarters of the year, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Birds that could give the coarsest cry

indicators.note: could give suggests the letters of the following words can be rearranged to yield something new

explanation.surface: Some birds are known for a particularly rough and raucous call.
explanation.definitionFit: These are black-and-white wading birds of the shore, an example of the general class named.

clue.text: It's humble, our appearance

parts.note: to demean someone is to humble or lower them

explanation.surface: Someone admits that their outward look is modest and unassuming.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing or outward manner is how a person comes across to others, their look and conduct.

clue.text: Person without clothes should receive good poke

indicators.note: should receive says the word for the unclothed person takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a nude is a person wearing nothing

explanation.surface: A naked person ought to get a playful jab, as if at a nudist camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle prod with the elbow is a small poke given to attract attention.

clue.text: Heart that's hollow and hard

parts.note: a pit is a hollow in the ground
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone's heart is described as both empty and unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow and hard' reads as a description of the heart, but they are two pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or essential part of something, as in the crux of an argument, is its heart.

clue.text: One sort of egg I consumed as pioneer

parts.note: one is written as the Roman numeral I
a nit is the egg of a louse
ate means consumed, eaten

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to eating an unusual egg as a trailblazing act.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer something is to start it off, to set it going first.

clue.text: Report of old servant not coming out of factory?

indicators.note: report of says the word for the old servant is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a handmaid is an old-fashioned word for a female servant

explanation.surface: A tale of a former servant who never left the mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods crafted by a person's own skill, rather than mass-produced by machine, are not factory products.

clue.text: Performed passionately, but took silly risks?

definitions.meaning: literal sense: acted or played music with real fire and feeling

explanation.surface: An actor gave a fiery performance but was reckless in doing so.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, performing with fire is playing with passion; the idiom means flirting with danger.

clue.text: King Charles, foolish person grossly insensitive

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, the royal cipher for a King Charles
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A king named Charles is called a dim and thoroughly tactless man.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude and lacking any sensitivity or refinement, a synonym for stupidly tactless.

clue.text: Ornament of mine, a doll specially made

indicators.note: specially made says the letters of the words given are refashioned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone owns a decorative piece, a doll made to order.
explanation.definitionFit: A large decorative pendant or circular relief is a kind of ornament.

clue.text: Couple study active intestinal parts

parts.note: a duo is a couple, a pair
a den is a study, a private room
A is the grammar abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: Two people examine the energetic workings of the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the first sections of the small intestine, plural of the anatomical term.

clue.text: Cathedral with endless music playing, a happy place

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, standard for cathedral

indicators.note: playing suggests the remaining letters are rearranged, as if in play
endless says the word music loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A cathedral with music that never stops would be a blissful place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts MUSIC to MUSI, then 'playing' rearranges it to SIUM. ELY is an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is the paradise of the blessed dead, so any state of bliss.

clue.text: Adjusted and put up

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is adapted to fit circumstances; the other is housed guests for the night.

clue.text: Within blend new ode is set to music

indicators.note: within says the rearranged words go inside the word for blend

parts.note: to meld is to blend

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of the following words are made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A poem is mixed into a fresh blend and then put to a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blend' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym; 'new' is the anagram indicator, and 'Within' puts its result inside the blend word.
explanation.definitionFit: To give words a tune is to compose a melody for them, putting verse into song.

clue.text: Namely, a loud lot of sheep in a metal frame?

parts.note: SC is scilicet, Latin for namely
F is forte, loud in music
a fold is a flock of sheep, or their pen

explanation.surface: A noisy flock of sheep is penned inside a metal enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: SC stands for the Latin scilicet, 'namely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders' temporary framework of poles and planks is typically metal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Most odd, as before, joining in pursuit

indicators.note: joining in says the word for before goes inside the word for pursuit

parts.note: a quest is a pursuit or search
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Something is described as the strangest, as earlier, for joining a chase.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer is an old word for odd, so the superlative means the oddest of all.

clue.text: Amount cleric squandered opposing submission

indicators.note: squandered suggests the letters are scattered wastefully and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A sum of money wasted by a churchman is contested by a legal claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim made in response to another's, opposing it, is a counter submission in law.

clue.text: A right girl to be followed by one sheep!

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A good girl is followed around by a single sheep, nursery-rhyme style.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wild Asian sheep with huge curled horns, a member of the class named.

clue.text: Making request in the role of top man

parts.note: as means in the role of, as in acting as chairman
a king is the top man of a realm

explanation.surface: Someone makes a demand while acting as the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a question or request to someone is the act described, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Flood shown in new film

parts.note: fresh means new
ET is the Spielberg film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A deluge is depicted in a newly released movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rise in a river from rain or melting snow is a small flood.

clue.text: As part of jaunt, I'd always like the sea

indicators.note: As part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: On a pleasure trip, someone says they have always loved the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea rises and falls with the pull of the moon, so it has tides.

clue.text: Shifts what's on herds?

indicators.note: shifts says the letters of the words that follow are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer asks what the job is of removing the things that sit on cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: 'Shifts' rearranges ON HERDS, and read as a whole it describes removing horns, the things on top of herds.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers remove horns from cattle, so the verb means taking away what grows on the animals' heads.

clue.text: Disregards orders I've put out

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are thrown into disarray and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that commands they issued have been ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside or overrule someone's decision is to ignore it in favour of one's own.

clue.text: I run to meet a queen, one from Asian land

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Q is the abbreviation for queen, as in chess notation
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to greet a royal visitor from a country in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one from Asian land' looks like the definition, but 'one' supplies the final I; the definition is the adjective 'from Asian land'.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a native or product of the Middle Eastern country whose capital is Baghdad.

clue.text: Appointment to give some blood at eleven

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A donor is booked in to give some blood at eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed engagement at a set time is an arrangement to meet, a synonym.

clue.text: Little bird to dart across sill

indicators.note: across says the word for dart stretches over the word for sill, which goes inside it

parts.note: to fling is to dart or rush headlong
a ledge is a sill, as of a window

explanation.surface: A tiny bird flits across a windowsill.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird just able to fly is small and new to flight.
